name: 52429-longprefill-qwen3p6-35b-a3b-2gpu
hardware: 2x H100 80GB HBM3, two GPUs of one a3 node.
parallelism: TP=2, PP=1, DP=1, expert parallelism off -- two GPUs, one engine. TP=1 does not fit: 67.0 GiB of BF16 weights leave no room on an 80 GB card for a KV cache beside them.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=1, bounded at 200 requests / 1800 s safety, with a 10% warmup by completion and a 5% cooldown. The first 20 requests are dropped as warmup, leaving ~180 measured.
workload: `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets. Prompt exactly 4096 tokens; output exactly 8 tokens, because a first-token boundary is stamped only when a later token follows it and a 1-token output therefore has no readable TTFT. `request_format: plain` with `temperature: 0.0`; prompts are Faker-generated synthetic English, freshly sampled per request.
purpose: A long-document analysis assistant on a 35-billion-parameter model, serving one user at a time 4,000-token prompts across two GPUs.
launch:
# vLLM at commit 5426311d9115c597c561967ec3f277ee6e970420. The interpreter, the CUDA
# forward-compatibility path and the hardware seal are in configs/env.yaml, which is this
# machine's and is not portable.
model: Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B

tensor-parallel-size: 2
pipeline-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 8192

# Must stay at or above the 4096-token prompt length. Below it the prefill is split across
# scheduler steps and TTFT becomes a count of those rather than the cost of one forward pass.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

# Sizes the per-sequence state pool (~30 MiB per sequence per rank), not the offered load.
# The engine default would reserve GiB of budget for slots one stream never uses.
max-num-seqs: 128

# A BUDGET, NOT A TARGET, AND DELIBERATELY BELOW THE 0.9 DEFAULT. What this configuration
# actually needs per rank is ~33.5 GiB of weights (67.0 GiB at TP=2), ~3.8 GiB of per-sequence
# recurrent state (128 slots x ~30 MiB), ~1.5 GiB of CUDA/NCCL context and under 2 GiB of
# activations for a single 8192-token batch -- about 41 GiB. The KV cache for the 10 full-attention
# layers is ~10 KiB per token per rank, so one 8192-token sequence needs 80 MiB of it. 0.65 of
# 79.19 GiB is 51.5 GiB, which clears that floor by ~10 GiB.
#
# 0.9 asks for 71.27 GiB of a card that has 79.19, i.e. it demands the GPU be within 8 GiB of
# empty, and vLLM refuses AT STARTUP if it is not. On a shared node that turned into the single
# most common way this item died. Nothing here is a performance knob: at one stream with a
# 4096-token prompt the pool is never more than a fraction full, so its size cannot move TTFT.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.65
